note: Written by scripts/analyze_observer_layer.py. Offsets are simulation minus observation in log10 number density per dex, the number the Explorer shows. This shows how much of an offset a given scatter could absorb; it does not show that the scatter exists in any survey.

settings.pairRule: sim_highline.compatible (the rules of compare.js) is not 'not-comparable', both records rankable; epochs: gap between the two redshift ranges at most max(0.15, 0.1 (1 + z_sim)); populations equal when both are stated
settings.classification: an offset is 'larger' when |median offset| > the median observational 1-sigma (yHigh-y or y-yLow, the larger) over the bins compared; pairs whose observed curve has no uncertainty are not classified
settings.scatterAppliedTo: the simulation curve only; the observed curve is untouched
settings.interiorOnly: the same, after removing the bins where more than edgeFlag of the scattered density comes from the continuation beyond the curve (before and after on the same bins)

unconvertedDifferences.note: |3 log10(H0_sim / H0_obs)|, the size of the Hubble-constant difference in number density that the comparison rules report and nobody converts here (over the comparable pairs before the bin-count filter)

changeInLog10DensityFromScatter.note: scattered minus input, at the points of the simulation curves in the measured pairs, bins flagged edge left out; percentiles, because a few far-tail points of fitted curves (density 1e-20 or less) change by tens of dex and mean nothing
